haiku-low.q1: The scheduler at 02:00 UTC (or 15 min after a failed attempt). It extracts replica orders with updated_at after the window start, HWM minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk-import transactions stay open up to 90 minutes; updated_at is set at write, not commit. So rows appear up to 90 minutes late.
haiku-low.q3: The edit has a newer updated_at, so the next night's 2-hour lookback extracts it and the merge updates the row.
haiku-low.q4: Its fact_orders row gets is_deleted set to true. The row is kept and never removed.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt ends and the merge rolls back; HWM stays put and etl_runs is marked failed. Retry after 15 minutes; attempt 3 failure pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 showing the previous complete load, since fact_orders is unchanged. The check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: A Sunday reconciliation compares counts and checksums per creation day over 30 days; a mismatched day is reloaded from the replica and merged.
haiku-low.q8: The merge keeps one row per order_id with greatest updated_at, and updates existing rows only when the staged updated_at is greater.
haiku-low.q9: etl_watermark (one row). Set to the cutoff recorded before the extract query runs, inside the merge transaction, only on commit.
haiku-low.q10: The merge is one warehouse transaction: steps 4a to 4e all commit or all roll back. Dashboards see the previous or new complete load.
haiku-low.q11: Staged rows are discarded: stg_orders is emptied at start of every attempt. The retry uses the same window, since the HWM did not move.
haiku-low.q12: Every order created that day, read from the replica ignoring the window. Merged by step 4 rules in its own transaction; HWM never changes.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC. It extracts every order in the replica whose updated_at is later than the window start (HWM minus 2 hours).
sonnet.q2: A bulk-import transaction in the app can stay open up to 90 minutes, and the app sets updated_at when it writes the row, not at commit. So the row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit sets a newer updated_at. The next nightly run's extract (updated_at after HWM minus 2 h) picks it up, and the merge updates the fact_orders row because the staged updated_at is greater than the stored one.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at (the row is not removed). The pipeline extracts it as a write with a newer updated_at, merges it, and sets is_deleted to true. The row stays in fact_orders and is never removed.
sonnet.q5: The attempt ends; a merge failure rolls back so data and the HWM don't change; an extract failure leaves only staging rows. Its etl_runs row is set to failed. Attempts 2 and 3 start 15 minutes after the previous failure. Success ends retries with no page; if attempt 3 fails, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh anyway and show the previous complete load. At 06:00 the check finds no committed run in etl_runs and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. The check does not stop or change the job.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares per-creation-day count and checksum (last 30 days) between replica and warehouse, and reloads mismatched days (provided Sunday night's load committed). Until then, nothing else picks it up.
sonnet.q8: Merge step 4a reduces staging to one row per order_id keeping the greatest updated_at. Step 4b's MERGE updates an existing fact_orders row only when the staged updated_at is greater than the stored one, and inserts new order_ids, so an older or duplicate copy never overwrites a newer one and re-running a window changes nothing.
sonnet.q9: In the etl_watermark table in the warehouse (one row). The value written is the new cutoff, the current time recorded in step 2 before the extract query runs. It is written in merge step 4d, inside the merge transaction, only if the attempt commits.
sonnet.q10: The merge (4a to 4e) is a single warehouse transaction that commits entirely or rolls back, so dashboards see either the previous complete load or the new complete load, never a partial one.
sonnet.q11: Staging is emptied at the start of the next attempt (before the extract) so it holds only that attempt's rows. A failed merge rolled back, so the HWM did not move, and the retry extracts the same window (HWM minus 2 hours).
sonnet.q12: It re-reads every order created that day from the replica, ignoring the window. The rows are merged using the same rules as step 4 (latest updated_at wins) in their own transaction. It never changes the HWM.
